profile.background: A 51-year-old adult lives in a studio and grows herbs on the fire escape. Visits a sister in the same neighborhood.
profile.history: Followed in an outpatient clinic for schizophrenia. At a stressful point last winter, several familiar voices seemed to overlap. The experience is now infrequent.
profile.organization: One detail can call up a loosely related memory before the original point is finished. Usually recalls the question and can return to it.
profile.spontaneity: Likes to tell stories about the neighborhood. Sometimes needs a moment to pick one of several recent events.
profile.guardedness: Comfortable discussing daily life and clinic care. Hesitant about the strain last winter put on the relationship with the sister.
profile.expression: Friendly and expressive. An aside can interrupt an otherwise understandable account. Moderately talkative. Uses several short clauses or a short anecdote about a familiar activity.
profile.self_understanding: Notices that conversations get harder to follow when tired. Can describe how sleep and evening company feel different.

facts.content: Walks to the sister’s flat most Saturdays and trades herbs for leftovers.
Has started waking once around dawn on some mornings, then usually gets back to sleep.
Last heard the overlapping voices about three weeks ago in the evening while alone.
On the last visit, the sister set aside a basil pot and the two of them repotted it after lunch.
facts.disclosure_context: A recent visit or an activity done together.

facts.content: Picks up a box of tablets from the pharmacy every four weeks. Has the refill date written inside the kitchen cupboard.
Can lose the thread of a family conversation when tired. Repotting the plant with the sister felt easy.
facts.disclosure_context: Attention in conversations and practical tasks.

facts.content: Thinks a shorter afternoon visit fits current energy better than staying through dinner.

dialogue.question: What was one part of this past weekend that you remember well?
dialogue.answer: “Repotting a basil plant with my sister comes to mind. She’d set the pot aside, and we did it together after lunch. I grow herbs on my fire escape, too. It felt easy, just doing something together.”

dialogue.question: How have your mornings and evenings felt lately?
dialogue.answer: “I’ve been waking around dawn some mornings, but I usually get back to sleep. With my sister, a shorter afternoon visit feels more manageable than staying through dinner. I like the company—it’s just harder to follow the conversation when I’m tired.”

dialogue.question: Has it been happening often?
dialogue.answer: Do you mean waking around dawn, or losing the thread when I’m talking with my sister?

dialogue.question: Let me ask more clearly. How often do you wake up earlier than you want to?
dialogue.answer: Some mornings I wake once around dawn, earlier than I’d like, but I usually get back to sleep.

dialogue.question: What sort of contact have you had with family in the last couple of weeks?
dialogue.answer: “Mostly visits with my sister—she’s in the same neighborhood. I walk over most Saturdays and take some herbs, and she gives me leftovers to bring home. Last time we repotted that basil together. A shorter afternoon visit suits me better just now; I still enjoy seeing her.”

dialogue.question: Can you give me an example of something you did the last time you spent time with someone?
dialogue.answer: “My sister and I repotted that basil plant after lunch on my last visit. She’d set the pot aside for us. I grow herbs on my fire escape too, so it was something familiar—it felt easy doing that together.”

dialogue.question: How have you been getting on with conversations and with hands-on activities?
dialogue.answer: “If I’m tired, I can lose the thread of a conversation with my sister. I still enjoy the company, but a shorter afternoon visit suits me better. Repotting that basil together felt easy, though. I grow herbs at home, so it was something familiar.”

dialogue.question: Which part takes longer to get back into?
dialogue.answer: “The conversation is harder to follow when I’m tired—I can lose the thread with my sister. Repotting the basil together felt easy, though.”

dialogue.question: I was thinking of conversation. When your attention wanders, how is it to pick up what someone is saying?
dialogue.answer: “When I’m tired, it’s harder to pick up the thread again. I still enjoy talking with my sister, but I can lose track of what she’s saying.”

dialogue.question: What arrangements, if any, do you make for collecting your medication?
dialogue.answer: I pick up a box of tablets from the pharmacy every four weeks. I’ve got the refill date written inside the kitchen cupboard, so I can check when it’s due.

dialogue.question: Thinking about your evenings again, have you noticed any sounds or voices that you found unusual?
dialogue.answer: Yes, about three weeks ago, one evening when I was alone. I heard familiar voices overlapping, several at once. That happened last winter too, but it’s infrequent now.

dialogue.question: If you were arranging your next family visit, what time of day would suit you?
dialogue.answer: “Afternoon would suit me best—a shorter visit with my sister, rather than staying through dinner. I enjoy seeing her, but conversation is harder to follow when I’m tired.”
